jobs.description:
At Whole Foods Market, we are working to nourish people and the planet. In this role, you will support the Team Leader in leading and executing the Customer Service & E-Commerce programs; this means you are responsible for the checkout experience and grocery delivery & pickup at your assigned store. You will focus on driving safety, quality of outbound online orders, excellent pickup experience, team productivity, and program execution. You will monitor key performance indicator metrics and visual cues in-store to assess the Team’s performance in these areas. You are responsible for daily operations including managing capacity, labor utilization, adherence to pick processes, and drop of task execution (for E-Commerce); and, cash management, customer demand management, labor utilization, and execution of store processes (for Customer Service). You may be responsible for aspects of managing non-inventory supplies management & expense control. You are responsible for regulatory compliance, and special projects and/or assignments. As the Associate Team Leader, you support the Team Leader in leading and developing Team Members. You may participate in hiring activities. You must strive to support WFM core values, Leadership Principles, and goals, promote national, geographic-specific, store programs and initiatives, and ensure adherence to all applicable health and safety regulations.

Establishes clear expectations for balancing in-store customer service and completing online orders.

Sustains strong knowledge and awareness of relevant competitors and industry trends.
Ensures an effective and efficient response to customer questions, requests, and/or concerns.

Fosters and encourages a positive environment of outstanding teamwork, mutual respect, and exceptional morale.
Maintains Team Member safety and security standards.
Ensures compliance with relevant regulatory rules and standards.
Develops, coaches, mentors, and motivates Team Members in a manner that sustains a high performing Team and minimizes turnover.
Maintains cleanliness of workspaces including staging area and coolers.
Maintains security of equipment, e.g., MSRs, phones, currency counters.
Proactively identifies process improvement opportunities.
Consistently communicates and models WFM core values, leadership principles, and supports goals.

Job Skills

Strong ability to perform task management, balancing dynamic customer flows.
Demonstrated understanding of how labor utilization and task management drive performance metrics and customer experience.
Strong analysis skills to root cause underperformance (either observed or demonstrated by metric performance).
Strong ability to communicate performance analysis findings and actions, both verbally and in writing.
Excellent interpersonal, motivational, team building and customer relationship skills.
Capable of teaching others in a positive and constructive manner.
Demonstrated decision-making ability, leadership skills, and ability to prioritize and delegate.
Proficient with email, Microsoft Office, and operations-related applications.
Proficient with mobile applications, dashboards, and basic understanding of retail systems capabilities.

18+ months retail experience including 6+ months of supervisory experience.

Position Description

Position Summary

The College of Health and Human Services (CHHS) is seeking an Administrative Support Coordinator II to provide centralized coordination and administrative support for graduate programs across the College, including its Joint Doctoral Programs (JDPs). Working closely with the Associate Dean for Research and Graduate Studies, this position helps keep critical graduate program processes, communications, records, and timelines organized and moving forward.

The Coordinator supports graduate programs throughout the student lifecycle—from recruitment and admissions through enrollment, academic progress, degree completion, and alumni follow-up. The position also provides dedicated administrative coordination for the Joint Doctoral Program in Interdisciplinary Research in Substance Use, including collaboration with UC San Diego, and contributes to Dean’s Office communications, events, and operations. This role is well suited for someone who excels at managing multiple priorities, navigating detailed administrative processes, building collaborative relationships, and ensuring important work is completed accurately and on time.

Key Responsibilities

Graduate Program Coordination: Coordinate administrative processes, timelines, records, and communications across CHHS graduate and Joint Doctoral Programs, ensuring required activities are completed accurately and on schedule.
Student Lifecycle Administration: Support processes spanning recruitment and admissions, enrollment, academic progress, degree completion, and alumni follow-up while maintaining organized records and tracking required actions.
Joint Doctoral Program Support: Provide dedicated administrative coordination for the Joint Doctoral Program in Interdisciplinary Research in Substance Use, including collaboration with UC San Diego and support for examinations, course agreements, documentation, and student processes.
Data & Records Coordination: Maintain graduate program tracking systems and coordinate the collection, organization, and reporting of student, alumni, academic, research, and career information in partnership with College and university units.
Communication & Stakeholder Support: Serve as a central administrative resource for program directors, faculty, students, alumni, staff, College leadership, and external partners by communicating established processes, coordinating follow-up, and connecting stakeholders with appropriate resources.
Administrative Problem Solving: Monitor deadlines and workflow, identify and resolve routine administrative issues, and coordinate with the Associate Dean or appropriate campus offices when matters require additional policy or program expertise.
Dean’s Office Operations: Support College communications and email management, special events, front-office functions, and other administrative projects that contribute to the academic and research operations of CHHS.

Why Join Us?

Support Graduate Student Success: Contribute to the graduate student experience from initial recruitment through degree completion and beyond.
Work Across Graduate Education: Build relationships with faculty, students, program directors, alumni, and partners across multiple graduate and doctoral programs.
Strengthen Program Coordination: Help create more connected, consistent, and effective graduate program operations across the College.
Gain Specialized Experience: Develop expertise in graduate and joint doctoral program administration, academic processes, data coordination, and cross-institutional collaboration.
Contribute to the CHHS Mission: Join a College committed to advancing research, education, and practice that address health and human service challenges in local, national, and global communities.

About Disability Law Group

At Disability Law Group, we exist for one reason: to help people through some of the most difficult moments of their lives — and to do that work with skill, heart, and purpose.

We are a mission-driven law firm focused on Social Security Disability

and Veterans’ disability benefits

. Our work demands more than legal knowledge; it requires empathy, persistence, and a genuine commitment to listening to people when they need it most.

Everything we do is guided by our core values — Listen, Invest, Vigor, Empathy, and Solutions (LIVES)

. These values shape how we show up for our clients and for one another. From the first phone call to the final resolution of a case, we treat each client’s situation as unique and deserving of thoughtful, personalized advocacy.

Our team is made up of dedicated professionals across intake, applications and appeals, records, case management, attorneys, and leadership, all working collaboratively to deliver exceptional service nationwide.

We also believe in investing in our people. DLG offers competitive pay and benefits

, meaningful opportunities for growth and advancement

, and a workplace culture that values balance and recognition — including a paid day off for your birthday

, team celebrations, and firm-wide KPIs. Our team regularly participates in community clinics, scholarship initiatives, and volunteer opportunities

, giving everyone the chance to make an impact beyond their day-to-day work. We also offer a flexible hybrid work

, and a family-first, model.

At Disability Law Group, your work matters — and so do you. Together, we are building a firm that delivers results, supports its people, and truly changes lives

About The Role

Are you someone who loves to connect with others? Can your circle of friends count on you to be that listening ear, always there and with the most heartfelt advice? Then look no further! Case Managers manage our clients’ cases from start to finish. Our case managers take great pride in the degree of client contact and case involvement they are able to experience each day. Each Case Manager works alongside a specific attorney to create a deeper sense of understanding and investment in each client’s unique situation. This position offers a great deal of independence, flexibility for personal styles, and responsibility over case files.

Key Responsibilities

Must be fluent in ARABIC
Preparing and submitting medical documents at each stage of the disability process.
Speaking with clients to address their case status, medical updates, and questions.
Communicating with Disability Determination Services, Social Security Field Offices, and the Office of Hearings Operations (OHO) to make sure the case is proceeding accordingly.
Maintain close communication with partnered attorney(s) to assure information is accurate and updated regarding the client and their case.
Answer/make calls regarding medical record review and file preparation.

What You'll Do

As a Case Manager, you will play a vital role in supporting our clients through the Social Security disability claims process. You will ensure seamless communication, meticulous case management, and timely follow-ups to help clients navigate this critical journey. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

Client Communication: Maintain daily communication with clients and the Social Security Administration (Field Offices, Disability Determination Services, Office of Hearing Operations, Appeals Council) to provide updates and address questions.
Document Coordination: Email Work Product (WP) to clients along with Medical Source Statements (MSS) and log all incoming mail and faxes, including hardship proofs, client letters, and other important documents.
Case File Management: Submit medical records and MSS to DDS/OHO, transfer documentation to appropriate offices (FO/OHO), and upload briefs via Electronic Records Express (ERE).
Hearing Preparation: Conduct final development calls for upcoming hearings, request and follow up on medical records two weeks prior to hearings and after, and ensure all necessary documentation is in place.
Decision Monitoring: Regularly check ERE for updates and decisions from Administrative Law Judges (ALJ) and the Appeals Council, set follow-up steps, and route decisions to appropriate channels for further action.
Status Checks: Perform status checks on pre-hearing files 30 days after submission to confirm receipt and accuracy of the appeal (501), resetting follow-up tasks every 60 days as needed.
Process Improvement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to streamline case workflows and enhance client experiences.

This position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and a client-first mindset. Your efforts will directly impact the lives of individuals seeking Social Security disability benefits.

Education and Experience:

High school diploma or equivalent; an associate’s or bachelor’s degree in social work, legal studies, or related field preferred.
At least one year of experience in case management, social services, or customer service.

Skills:

Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple cases and deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and case management software.
Attention to detail in preparing and reviewing medical documents.

Interpersonal Abilities:

Empathy and patience when working with clients with disabilities.
Ability to build strong professional relationships with clients, attorneys, and agency representatives.

Problem-Solving:

Proactive in addressing case issues and resolving client concerns.
Knowledge of Social Security disability processes or willingness to learn.

Desired Qualifications

Familiarity with Social Security disability claims and legal processes.
Preferred experience with USDC cases

Technical Skills:

Experience with electronic medical records (EMR) or CRM systems.

Community Focus:

Engagement in volunteerism or advocacy for underserved populations.

What You'll Do

As a Case Manager, you will play a vital role in supporting our clients through the Social Security disability claims process. You will ensure seamless communication, meticulous case management, and timely follow-ups to help clients navigate this critical journey. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

Client Communication: Maintain daily communication with clients and the Social Security Administration (Field Offices, Disability Determination Services, Office of Hearing Operations, Appeals Council) to provide updates and address questions.
Document Coordination: Email Work Product (WP) to clients along with Medical Source Statements (MSS) and log all incoming mail and faxes, including hardship proofs, client letters, and other important documents.
Case File Management: Submit medical records and MSS to DDS/OHO, transfer documentation to appropriate offices (FO/OHO), and upload briefs via Electronic Records Express (ERE).
Hearing Preparation: Conduct final development calls for upcoming hearings, request and follow up on medical records two weeks prior to hearings and after, and ensure all necessary documentation is in place.
Decision Monitoring: Regularly check ERE for updates and decisions from Administrative Law Judges (ALJ) and the Appeals Council, set follow-up steps, and route decisions to appropriate channels for further action.
Status Checks: Perform status checks on pre-hearing files 30 days after submission to confirm receipt and accuracy of the appeal (501), resetting follow-up tasks every 60 days as needed.
Process Improvement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to streamline case workflows and enhance client experiences.

This position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and a client-first mindset. Your efforts will directly impact the lives of individuals seeking Social Security disability benefits.
